## 1. Two ways to use this course

::: {.grid}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### In the browser — nothing to install
Most lessons in Levels 1–3 contain **interactive exercises**: code boxes you can edit and run directly on the page (powered by [webR](https://docs.r-wasm.org/webr/latest/), R compiled for the browser). Click **Run Code**, use **Hint** when you are stuck and **Show Solution** to compare.

The first exercise on a page can take a few seconds while R starts in your browser.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### On your computer — recommended
To follow every lesson, work on your own data and complete the [capstone project](lessons/67-capstone.qmd), install R and an editor (below). It is free and takes a few minutes.
:::
:::

## 2. Install R (version 4.5 or newer)

Download R from **CRAN**, the official repository: <https://cran.r-project.org>. Choose your operating system and follow the installer.

::: {.callout-note}
## Why R ≥ 4.5?
The course uses the `penguins` dataset that ships with R since version 4.5.0. Check your version by typing `R.version.string` in the R console.
:::

## 3. Install an editor (IDE)

You can use either:

- **RStudio Desktop** — the classic, very popular IDE: <https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/>
- **Positron** — Posit's newer data-science IDE (R and Python): <https://positron.posit.co>

Both are free. Lesson [1](lessons/01-foundations/01-what-is-r.qmd) gives a short tour of the RStudio panes; Positron is organised in a similar way.

## 4. Install the course packages

Open R (or your IDE) and run this single line. It installs every package used in the course (it may take 10–20 minutes the first time):

```r
source("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gianluca-sottile/An-R-Tutorial-for-Beginners/master/scripts/install-packages.R")
```

The optional deep-learning track needs additional software; [Lesson 61](lessons/13-deep-learning/61-dl-setup.qmd) explains how to install it.

## 5. How a lesson is organised

```{=html}
<div class="lesson-meta"><span class="level-2">Level 2 · Describe &amp; explore</span><span>⏱ ~60 min</span><span>Prerequisites: …</span></div>
```

Every lesson starts with its **level**, an **estimated time** and its **prerequisites**, then:

| Block | What it is for |
|---|---|
| 🎯 **Learning objectives** | What you will be able to do at the end |
| 💡 **Why…?** | The real problem the method solves |
| ▶️ **Code + explanation** | Short chunks, each explained |
| 🔎 **How to read this output** | Line-by-line guide to R's results |
| 🔬 **Going deeper** (collapsed) | Formulas and theory for those who want them |
| ⚠️ **Common pitfalls** | Frequent mistakes and misconceptions |
| ✅ **Check your understanding** | Quick questions with hidden answers |
| ✍️ **Exercises** ★ / ★★ / ★★★ | Increasing difficulty, solutions included |
| 📋 **Summary** | Key functions and ideas at a glance |

Code you can copy has a copy button in its top-right corner. Output lines start with `#>`.

## 6. Suggested routes

| You are… | Suggested route |
|---|---|
| Completely new to R and statistics | All lessons in order, Level 1 → 4 |
| Comfortable with R, rusty on statistics | Skim Level 1, then Levels 2–3 carefully |
| Know statistics, new to R | Level 1, then lessons 24–27 (graphics), then Level 4 |
| Need machine learning quickly | 08–10, 18, 24, 38–41, then 44–49 |

See the full [learning path](learning-path.qmd) for the map of prerequisites.

## 7. For instructors and contributors: working with the source

The website is a [Quarto](https://quarto.org) project. To build it locally:

1. Install [Quarto](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/) (≥ 1.6) and the course packages (step 4).
2. Clone the repository and open `An-R-Tutorial-for-Beginners.Rproj`.
3. In the terminal, once: `quarto add r-wasm/quarto-live` (installs the interactive-exercise extension; commit the `_extensions/` folder).
4. Preview with `quarto preview`; build everything with `quarto render`.

All R results are stored in `_freeze/` (Quarto's **freeze** feature), which is committed to git. GitHub Actions then publishes the site **without running R**, so heavy computations (including deep learning) only ever run on your own computer.

Found an error? Use the **"Report an issue"** link at the bottom of the table of contents on any page.
